summary: Configured persistent SSH key-based access for opsbot from node1 to node2. Password authentication is disabled, both accounts are locked, and both nodes recovered successfully after sequential restarts. CentOS 5.11 and kernel 2.6.18-398.el5 remain unchanged.
actions_performed: Created opsbot on node1 and node2 with locked passwords.
Generated a legacy-compatible 2048-bit RSA key on node1 and authorized it on both nodes.
Set PasswordAuthentication no and PubkeyAuthentication yes, validated the configuration, and reloaded sshd.
Verified key-authenticated command execution as opsbot on both nodes and rejection of password-only authentication.
Restarted node1 and node2 individually, proving changed boot identities and full recovery after each restart.

evidence.requirement: Create secured opsbot accounts on both systems
evidence.summary: opsbot exists as UID 501 on both nodes with locked passwords and protected SSH directories.
node2 authorized_keys has mode 600, opsbot ownership, and the expected 2048-bit key.

evidence.requirement: Run commands from node1 as opsbot on node2 and require key authentication
evidence.summary: Key-authenticated commands succeed as opsbot UID 501 on both nodes; password-only attempts are rejected with only publickey/GSSAPI offered.

evidence.requirement: Preserve installed OS release and kernel
evidence.summary: Before and after restarts, both nodes report CentOS 5.11 and kernel 2.6.18-398.el5.
Healthy baseline; reboot acknowledged with boot ID dd6182fa-…; recovered with changed boot ID 5f5639d7-…, running SSH, persistent account/key/configuration, and working key access.
Healthy baseline; reboot acknowledged with boot ID ffbd23b0-…; recovered with changed boot ID 3432036d-…, running SSH, persistent account/key/configuration, and successful node1-to-node2 key access.
